transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Mike Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (CTO, Nimbus), Elena Park (Head of Security, Nimbus), Samir Khan (DevOps, Nimbus)

Summary:
Quick run through of encryption at rest/in-transit, KMS options including BYOK and HSM, audit logging and retention, and how Redwood supports private deployments and key management. Agreement to share certs and schedule a dedicated-pool benchmark.

Topics:
- Encryption at rest vs in transit
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM integration
- Key rotation and rotation policies
- Audit logs and retention / export
- Data residency & private deployment options
- Next steps: docs and benchmark scheduling

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, I'm the account lead. With me is Mike, our SE, he'll cover the HSM and KMS bits.
[00:12] Carlos: Hey all, Carlos here, thanks. Elena and Samir are on as well.
[00:17] Elena: Hi.
[00:19] Mike: Hi team. Quick call goal - we want to make sure Nimbus's encryption and key-management controls map to your security requirements.
[00:27] Carlos: Yep, this is for our payments platform so we need to be strict. We got questions from legal on BYOK and how keys are used for models, and, um, how audit logs work.
[00:37] Aisha: Great. Mike, do you want to start with how we do encryption at rest and in transit?
[00:42] Mike: Sure. So, at a high level, all network traffic to Redwood is TLS 1.2/1.3 by default - that covers in-transit. For at-rest, we use AES-256 for disk encryption. In the hosted offering the master keys are managed by Redwood by default, but we support customer-managed keys - BYOK - via KMS integration.
[01:05] Elena: When you say KMS integration, which providers do you support? Is HSM required?
[01:09] Mike: We out-of-the-box integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For HSM-backed keys we can integrate with cloud HSM offerings (e.g. AWS CloudHSM) or on-prem HSM via key-wrapping. The main pattern we use is envelope encryption: data keys are wrapped by the customer key in KMS/HSM.
[01:30] Samir: So the data keys used by the runtime are ephemeral and not stored in plaintext?
[01:34] Mike: Correct - the runtime holds the unwrapped data key in memory only for the duration needed, it's not written to disk. We also support hardware isolation on Dedicated/Private deployments to reduce exposure.
[01:45] Elena: How about key rotation? We have policies for rotating every 90 days and need to ensure backwards decryption for older data.
[01:52] Mike: We support key rotation workflows - you can schedule rotation in your KMS and Redwood will fetch the new wrapping key. For older encrypted artifacts, we maintain key metadata to locate the correct wrapping key so objects remain decryptable. If you use BYOK with HSM, rotation is handled in the HSM and we reference the correct wrapping key ID.
[02:10] Carlos: Is there any chance Redwood or a third-party could export the unwrapped key? We need to ensure our key material never lands outside our control.
[02:18] Mike: If you're in the hosted model with Redwood-managed keys, Redwood controls the master key, so we can decrypt for operations like backup restores per our legal process. With BYOK, the master WRAPPING key lives in your KMS/HSM - Redwood never has the plaintext master key. For HSM integrations we can do a key-wrapping exchange - essentially you provide the public key to encrypt the data key.
[02:40] Elena: Ok, and what's the process for key compromise or forced rotation?
[02:44] Mike: If you suspect compromise, you rotate the wrapping key in your KMS/HSM. For data encrypted with the compromised wrapping key, you'd rewrap with a new key - we provide tooling to assist rewraps. We also have playbooks for incident response, and we can produce audit logs for all key unwrap/wrap operations.
[03:02] Samir: Speaking of audit logs, what events are captured and what's retention? We need to show to auditors who accessed keys and when.
[03:09] Mike: We capture request-level logs: key wrap/unwrap attempts, API calls that resulted in decryption, and administrative actions. Logs include timestamp, principal, operation, request id. By default logs are retained for 90 days in hosted, but for enterprise customers you can extend retention or export logs to your SIEM - we support secure push to S3/GCS/Azure Blob or send via syslog/ELK ingestion.
[03:33] Elena: Is there any PII in the logs? We prefer logs to avoid full payloads.
[03:37] Mike: We scrub payloads; logs have metadata only. We do log hash identifiers for tracing without containing cleartext.
[03:44] Carlos: For compliance, we need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts.
[03:48] Aisha: Absolutely - we'll send our certs and the most recent penetration test summary.
[03:52] Elena: Great. Another legal ask was around data residency - can you guarantee keys and data remain in our EU region?
[03:59] Mike: On hosted we have region options and you can pin storage to a region. For the strictest needs we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with region-specific pools - keys stay in the region KMS/HSM you control, as long as you provide keys in that region or use a cloud KMS instance there.
[04:19] Samir: If we go Private, does Redwood still see any telemetry?
[04:22] Mike: Private includes an option to run the control plane with customer-managed network - telemetry can be configured to forward to your collectors. You can also opt out of certain telemetry.
[04:32] Elena: Ok. Aish, sorry, Aisha, what's the difference operationally between BYOK and full HSM-backed BYOK?
[04:39] Aisha: I'll let Mike handle the deep-ops detail but from contract POV BYOK is you own the keys in your KMS; HSM-backed means those keys are protected by a dedicated hardware module. HSM adds FIPS validations and tamper-resistance.
[04:52] Mike: Right. With standard KMS keys you have CMEK with cloud provider protections. With HSM-backed keys the key material never leaves the HSM, and operations are done inside the module. For some auditors that's a requirement.
[05:05] Carlos: We also wanted to confirm tokenization and model caching behavior - does caching ever persist decrypted content to disk?
[05:13] Mike: No, KV cache is encrypted at rest with the same envelope-based approach. The runtime may cache prefixes in memory for performance; we never write unencrypted content to disk. Occasionally the transcript note: "K-V cache" can be mis-transcribed as "kay-vee cache" - but the point is it's memory-resident and encrypted when persisted.
[05:33] Elena: What about backups? Snapshots of state - how are they encrypted and who controls keys?
[05:38] Mike: Snapshots are encrypted with data keys and wrapped by your wrapping key when BYOK is used. For hosted, we rotate snapshots into Redwood-managed keys unless you provide BYOK. Backups can be exported to your storage if you prefer to hold snapshots yourself.
[05:52] Samir: Are you able to integrate with our HSM vendor, Thales, for example?
[05:56] Mike: Yes, by using an HSM that supports standard PKCS#11 or cloud HSM APIs we can integrate. For on-prem HSMs we do a key-wrapping exchange. We'll need network connectivity and IOPS considerations for latency.
[06:12] Carlos: Latency - does BYOK/HSM add measurable latency to inference?
[06:16] Mike: The unwrap operation happens during key retrieval; we cache unwrapped data keys in memory so runtime latency isn't impacted on a per-token basis. The initial unwrap or rotation has a small millisecond overhead. For HSMs there can be additional overhead if every operation is forced through HSM; we advise envelope encryption to minimize calls.
[06:34] Elena: Any recommendations for rotation cadence? We do 90 days for master keys, but for data keys we rotate more frequently?
[06:40] Mike: Common pattern: rotate wrapping/master keys on your 90 day cadence, rotate data keys more frequently depending on threat model. For ML artifacts, many customers rotate data keys monthly or on each model version deployment.
[06:52] Carlos: Is Redwood SOC2 scope inclusive of Dedicated and Private offerings?
[06:56] Aisha: Our SOC2 report primarily covers our hosted control plane and managed services. For Dedicated and Private we provide a combination of our SOC2 plus deployment-specific attestations. We'll include an explanation in the docs we send.
[07:10] Samir: We saw a mention in the docs about RBAC and SSO - how granular is access control for key operations?
[07:16] Mike: We support RBAC at route and namespace level; you can bind SAML/SCIM groups to roles. For key operations we log admin actions and you can restrict key unwrap privileges to specific roles. For extra assurance you can enforce MFA and require approvals for key rotation.
[07:32] Elena: Nice. For audit reviews we need an exportable trail with immutable ordering. Is there an integrity guarantee?
[07:39] Mike: We provide signed log archives when requested; you can export to your own immutable storage (WORM) in your cloud and we can push there. That satisfies integrity requirements for many auditors.
[07:50] Carlos: Any gotchas for contract text about BYOK? We want guarantees that Redwood cannot access our plaintext keys.
[07:57] Aisha: We'll provide suggested contract clauses. The legal team typically takes: that Redwood will not store or export customer-owned wrapping keys, and that key operations are logged. For hosted customers there are carve-outs around operational needs; we'll send the exact wording.
[08:12] Elena: One more: HSM attestation - can you provide chain-of-custody or HSM attestation for keys generated in your environment?
[08:20] Mike: If keys are in your HSM, you control attestation. If using our HSM instances (e.g., CloudHSM) we can provide the cloud provider attestation artifacts. For on-prem HSMs, attestation is something your security team would perform locally.
[08:34] Samir: Sounds good. We want to run a pilot with BYOK and measure latency at scale. Can we schedule a benchmark on Dedicated with a pinned GPU pool?
[08:42] Aisha: Absolutely - we'll schedule the benchmark. We recommend starting with a 2-hour stress test at target throughput, then a longer soak.
[08:50] Carlos: Timeline wise, we want to sign PO by end of May if pilot looks good.
[08:54] Aisha: That's doable.
[08:56] Elena: Any other documents you can share? Key rotation playbook?
[09:00] Mike: Yes, we have a key rotation playbook and an HSM integration checklist. I'll share both.
[09:06] Aisha: Ok let's wrap up with next steps.
[09:09] Aisha: Action items - I'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test, Mike will send KMS/HSM guides and playbooks, and we'll get the benchmark scheduled for the week of May 4th.
[09:22] Carlos: Good, thanks everyone.
[09:24] Elena: Thank you.
[09:25] Samir: Thanks.
[09:27] Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email.

End of transcript
